 LPG Gas Market in Kenya: Can Household Demand Drive Distributor Growth? – Expert View by Spherical Insights
 RELEASE DATE: 
 Oct 2026 
 Author: 
 Spherical Insights 
 Kenya’s LPG demand rose almost 15% in 2025, and companies are investing in cylinders, smaller refills and retail outlets to reach more households. Affordability, new levies and illegal refilling remain barriers to growth.

 Speak to Analyst 
 Kenya’s LPG demand rose almost 15% in 2025, and companies are investing in cylinders, smaller refills and retail outlets to reach more households. Affordability, new levies and illegal refilling remain barriers to growth. 
 Kenya’s liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market is expanding as households, businesses and public institutions increasingly adopt cleaner cooking energy. LPG consumption reached 475,943 tonnes in 2025, up 14.7% from 414,861 tonnes in 2024, based on the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA). The government’s National LPG Growth Strategy aims to widen access through household cylinder distribution, LPG use in public learning institutions and infrastructure development. The State Department for Petroleum identifies 8.4 million households as the target for transition from traditional biomass fuels to LPG. These initiatives are creating opportunities for gas marketers, cylinder suppliers, retailers and last-mile delivery providers. As demand grows, investment in storage, distribution networks and affordable access will shape the market’s next phase.
 How Is LPG Demand Growing in Kenya? 
 Kenya's LPG consumption has maintained strong growth, increasing from 360,594 tonnes in 2023 to 414,861 tonnes in 2024, representing an annual rise of approximately 15%. The upward trend continued in 2025, when consumption reached 475,943 tonnes, an increase of 14.72%. Per-capita LPG consumption also increased from 7.9 kg to 8.9 kg during the same period, reflecting wider adoption of cooking gas.
 Government initiatives have supported this expansion. The 2023 tax changes, which introduced zero-rating for LPG, improved its affordability and encouraged wider adoption. The National LPG Growth Strategy has further supported demand through household cylinder distribution, LPG adoption in public learning institutions and expanded distribution infrastructure. Together, these developments are strengthening Kenya's LPG consumption and creating opportunities across the country's energy distribution network.
 What Is Driving Household Demand for LPG? 
 Three forces stand out. First, government policy: a National LPG Growth Strategy and clean-cooking programmes aim to move households away from charcoal and firewood. Second, tax treatment, since zero-rating lowered the cost of gas for several years. Third, product availability, as marketers offer smaller cylinders, cheaper refills and payment plans.
 The government aims to raise LPG penetration from 24% to 70% by 2028 and to plan for 10 million additional cylinders, with distribution details still under discussion. Clean cooking is also framed as a public health and climate measure, since it can reduce indoor air pollution and pressure on forests. Even so, low-income households often still rely on charcoal and firewood because gas remains costly.

 Key Statistics: 
 LPG Demand: Kenya's LPG demand reached 475,943 tonnes in 2025, representing a reported year-on-year increase of 14.7%.
 Per-Person Consumption: LPG consumption reached 7.9 kg per person in 2024/25, compared with 7.0 kg in 2023, according to the figures provided.
 Household Penetration Target: The government aims to increase LPG penetration from 24% to 70% by 2028. This remains a policy target rather than an achieved outcome.
 Per-Person Consumption Target: The government aims to raise annual LPG consumption to at least 15 kg per person, highlighting the scope for further growth.
 TotalEnergies Investment Plans: TotalEnergies plans to invest more than KSh 1 billion annually in LPG infrastructure and distribution, with a target of distributing 180,000–200,000 cylinders each year.
 LPG Levy: A levy of KSh 5.40 per kilogram was introduced through a 2025 amendment order. Its implications for retail prices and household affordability warrant attention.
 How Are Companies Expanding LPG Distribution? 
 TotalEnergies Marketing Kenya announced in June 2026 plans to invest more than KSh 1 billion annually in LPG infrastructure, cylinder distribution and flexible payment solutions. The company aims to distribute between 180,000 and 200,000 cylinders each year and add approximately one million new users annually. With an existing customer base reaching around four million people in Kenya, the company is strengthening its distribution network to expand access to liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and support the country's transition towards cleaner cooking fuels.
 Its expansion strategy combines digital technology, affordable payment options and community-based retail networks. Through its partnership with M-Gas, the pay-as-you-cook programme enables households to purchase LPG in small quantities using smart meters, with payments starting at KSh 9. More than 42,000 smart cylinders have been deployed, reaching an estimated 200,000 people. The company's Maskani retail network currently operates 42 outlets, with another 40 planned for 2026 to bring LPG services closer to residential communities.
 These investments highlight how flexible payment models, digital solutions and wider retail coverage can improve access to LPG. By making distribution more accessible and aligning purchases with household budgets, such initiatives could help expand the customer base, encourage repeat consumption and strengthen Kenya's clean-cooking market.
 Can Smaller Cylinders Make LPG More Affordable? 
 Smaller LPG cylinders can help households manage the upfront cost of switching to cleaner cooking fuels. In May 2026, TotalEnergies promoted its 3 kg Baby Meko cylinder with a KSh 700 refill offer targeting price-sensitive consumers. The initiative aims to make LPG more accessible to low-income households. Smaller refills allow families to purchase fuel according to their budgets, while wider adoption could expand the customer base. However, sustained growth will depend on refill prices, equipment costs and household purchasing power.
 Which Companies Are Shaping Kenya’s LPG Market? 
 TotalEnergies Marketing Kenya 
 TotalEnergies Marketing Kenya distributes LPG under its TotalEnergies GAS brand for domestic and commercial use. Its operations include cylinder sales, bulk supply and specialised delivery services through depots in Mombasa, Nairobi and Kisumu. The company is also expanding access through Maskani retail outlets and flexible payment initiatives.
 Rubis Energy Kenya 
 Rubis Energy Kenya markets cooking gas under its RUBiS GAS brand, serving households and commercial customers. Its products include 6 kg and 13 kg cylinders, available through service stations and authorised dealers. The company also supplies LPG to manufacturing businesses, schools, hospitals and hotels.
 Vivo Energy Kenya 
 Vivo Energy Kenya supplies LPG under its Afrigas brand, offering cylinder sizes including 6 kg, 13 kg, 25 kg and 45 kg. Its extensive retail network and established petroleum distribution infrastructure support access to cooking gas for households and commercial customers across Kenya.
 Proto Energy 
 Proto Energy is a Kenya-based LPG supplier specialising in household gas, bulk supply, cylinder manufacturing and refilling services. Its product portfolio includes LPG solutions for domestic and industrial customers. The company also provides opportunities for distributors to participate in its expanding gas distribution network.
 Taifa Gas Kenya 
 Taifa Gas is developing a KSh 16 billion LPG import and storage terminal at the Dongo Kundu Special Economic Zone in Mombasa. Designed for a storage capacity of 30,000 metric tonnes, the facility could strengthen bulk supply infrastructure, expand competition and improve distribution capacity once operational.
 Leading Companies in Kenya’s LPG Market 
 Safety and Illegal Refilling: Kenya recorded eight major LPG incidents in 2025, including a cylinder explosion in Nairobi's Githurai area that killed two residents. In August 2026, the government announced intensified enforcement against illegal refilling. A planned cylinder-tracking system is intended to improve traceability and strengthen safety across the supply chain.
 Taxation: The Petroleum Development Levy (Amendment) Order, 2025 introduced a levy of KSh 5.40 per kilogram of LPG. The Consumer Federation of Kenya raised concerns about its potential impact on household affordability and the country's clean-cooking objectives.
 Household Affordability: The upfront cost of cylinders, refill prices and distribution expenses can limit LPG adoption, particularly among low-income households. Smaller cylinders and flexible payment options offer potential ways to improve access.
 Regulatory Compliance: LPG distributors must meet licensing and safety requirements, including valid fire certificates, calibrated weighing scales and written consent from registered cylinder brand owners. These requirements support consumer safety while adding compliance responsibilities for legitimate operators.
 Import and Storage Concentration: Kenya's LPG supply chain faces concentration in import and storage infrastructure. Expanding storage capacity and developing additional supply facilities could create opportunities to diversify supply and strengthen competition, although the effect on retail prices will depend on operating costs, taxes and distribution margins.
 How Could New Infrastructure and Government Policies Shape Competition? 
 Import and storage infrastructure could strengthen Kenya’s LPG market. Taifa Gas’s planned Mombasa terminal is expected to expand storage capacity, improve supply flexibility and create opportunities for greater competition. These developments could support market growth and improve LPG accessibility.
 Government policies will also influence the industry’s development. The LPG levy, licensing framework and planned cylinder-tracking system will shape market operations. Proposed LPG infrastructure provisions in new housing developments could further encourage adoption and support Kenya’s transition towards cleaner cooking fuels.
 Safety initiatives are strengthening industry standards. Following eight major LPG incidents in 2025, EPRA reinforced safety requirements in February 2026. The regulator also reported two licence revocations during 2025. In August 2026, the Energy Cabinet Secretary announced intensified enforcement to promote safer LPG distribution.
 Future Outlook 
 Kenya’s LPG market is positioned for continued growth as clean-cooking initiatives, expanding distribution networks and flexible payment options improve household access. Planned investments in storage infrastructure could strengthen supply capacity and create new opportunities for distributors. Government policies supporting safety, cylinder traceability and LPG infrastructure in new housing developments may further shape industry development. Companies that combine affordable refills, reliable distribution and customer-focused solutions will be well positioned to capture emerging opportunities in Kenya’s evolving cooking-energy market.
 Conclusion 
 Kenya’s LPG market presents significant opportunities for distributors as households increasingly adopt cleaner cooking fuels. Investments in storage infrastructure, accessible cylinder options and flexible payment models could support wider adoption and strengthen market participation. Government initiatives focused on affordability, safety and distribution infrastructure will also influence the industry’s development. Companies that prioritise reliable supply, customer accessibility and regulatory compliance can strengthen their market positions. As Kenya advances its clean-cooking objectives, collaboration between policymakers and industry participants will be important for building a more accessible and sustainable LPG market.
